study type: Retrospective cohort study with a cross-sectional comparison
exposure: Pregnancy in women with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) who underwent correction surgery
outcome: Prevalence and severity of low back pain (during pregnancy and long-term after delivery)
cohort: The study included women aged 18-40 years who had undergone correction surgery for AIS, comparing those with a history of pregnancy to AIS patients without pregnancy and healthy women with a history of pregnancy.
finding: Women who underwent scoliosis correction suffered from long-term back pain after pregnancy, had decreased satisfaction with surgery, and experienced high rates of refusal for regional anesthesia during delivery.
mod_finding: The rates of regional anesthesia prescription among pregnant patients with AIS who underwent correction surgery was 30% (5/17), significantly lower than healthy pregnant women (100%).
followup_time: Long-term after delivery (exact duration not specified)
